heroSummary: The enclosed Bambu Lab P1S pairs exceptionally well with Polymaker PolyLite PETG, sustaining a 14 mm³/s volumetric flow ceiling for reliable 167 mm/s outer wall and infill speeds without thermal drafts or layer delamination.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Liquid Glue / Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Disable "Reduce infill retraction" in OrcaSlicer under Others → Special Mode to stop PETG blobs from accumulating on the nozzle tip during high-speed grid travel.
Switch infill pattern from Grid to Gyroid or 3D Honeycomb at 15% density so the nozzle never crosses existing extruded PETG lines on the same layer.
Set Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the Filament tab; stock Bambu Generic PETG profiles often push 18+ mm³/s which causes matte under-extrusion with PolyLite PETG.
Configure Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan to 0% for the entire print to eliminate asymmetric chamber drafts that cause corner lifting on large flat functional parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Wispy cobweb stringing on travel moves and Z-seams
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in hygroscopic PolyLite PETG combined with excessive nozzle dwell heat.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours before printing, set retraction length to 0.8mm at 35 mm/s, and enable Wipe while retracting (1.5mm wipe distance).

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Infill crumbs and nozzle scraping mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Crossing infill paths (Grid/Triangles) cause molten PETG buildup on the stainless steel nozzle cone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Change Sparse Infill Pattern to Gyroid, lower infill flow ratio to 0.96, and increase Z-hop when retracting to 0.4mm Spiral.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PETG fusing permanently to the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Direct high-temperature PETG bond with bare PEI coating during cooling contraction.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin barrier coat of liquid glue stick on the Textured PEI plate and let the bed cool below 40°C before flexing parts off.

faq.question: Do I need to open the Bambu Lab P1S door when printing Polymaker PolyLite PETG?
faq.answer: No. Unlike low-temp PLA which can suffer heat creep in a closed chamber, PolyLite PETG has a ~80°C glass transition temperature and prints cleanly with both the front door and top glass closed.

faq.question: Can I use Polymaker PolyLite PETG cardboard spools in the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: Modern PolyLite spools include factory sealed edge-glue that runs smoothly in the AMS, though printing snap-on plastic rim adapters prevents cardboard dust buildup on the AMS rollers.

faq.question: What is the ideal nozzle temperature for PolyLite PETG on the P1S?
faq.answer: 240°C is the sweet spot for balanced inter-layer adhesion and minimal stringing at 167 mm/s print speeds on the P1S all-metal hotend.

faq.question: Should I upgrade the stock P1S nozzle for Polymaker PolyLite PETG?
faq.answer: The stock 0.4mm Stainless Steel nozzle handles standard non-filled PolyLite PETG without accelerated wear, though upgrading to a Hardened Steel nozzle is recommended if you also print CF or glow variants.
